Companion Animal Travel Desk reply

The complaint describes that the traveler reported a minor injury to their pet during handling, followed by a delayed departure that extended the wait at the transfer point.

We acknowledge the concerns raised by Yara Okafor regarding Skye, and we are treating this as an incident that requires immediate operational review across the ground handling and departure workflow. Our ground team moves carriers carefully between services; however, when a traveler reports harm or discomfort, our priority is to verify the animal's condition, secure the right handling method for the remainder of the itinerary, and protect the connection integrity for the next segment.

On the reported minor injury, we have flagged the service record for carrier handling and station transfer, including the sequence of staff actions and the timing of carrier movement. The supervisor on duty is documenting the immediate response taken when the animal was found to be unsettled, and we are checking whether any deviation occurred in padding, restraint positioning, carrier closure verification, or transition routing. <<FACT F119>> Please note that the claim window begins at the point you first reported the issue to staff at the station, and any supporting documentation you can provide now will speed verification.

Regarding the delayed departure, we understand how distressing it is to experience an added wait after a concern about the pet. Our operations planning team is reviewing the departure clearance timeline for the affected service and matching it against the carrier transfer completion record. This review includes ground-to-air coordination, gate readiness confirmation, and any hold applied to maintain safe handling conditions during the transfer. <<FACT F109>> Your case has been marked for priority validation so that the standard process aligns with what occurred on the day in question.

If Amara Bennett or any additional representative assisted you at the terminal, include the name in your next message to ensure the notes match the correct point of contact. If you have medical documentation from a station veterinarian or any proof of observation, keep it available for attachment to the claim. Our supervisors are listening carefully when a passenger is worried, and we are assigning an incident coordinator to ensure you receive a single, consolidated status update rather than fragmented responses.

We appreciate your patience while our team completes the record reconciliation, and we will act on the findings with corrective steps where needed to prevent recurrence.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
